## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-cell-cell-communication-in-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-9-cellchat-analysis/>

Part 1 of 3. CellChat infers cell-cell communication from ligand and receptor
expression: for every pair of cell groups and every ligand-receptor pair in the
CellChatDB database it computes a communication probability, tests it by
permutation, and aggregates the result by signaling pathway.

This notebook runs the analysis for the **Healthy** condition only: build the
CellChat object, infer and aggregate the network, plot interactions and one
signaling pathway (MHC-II), find dominant senders and receivers, identify
global communication patterns (non-negative matrix factorization, NMF) and
group pathways by functional similarity. The object is saved for part 3. Part 2
repeats the inference for the Post_Treatment condition, and part 3 compares the
two.

**Input.** The article reads a downsampled Seurat object from Parts 7 / 7-2.
Here that is the object saved by tutorial 7 (Monocle 3) part 1,
`seurat_subset_downsampled.rds`, so **tutorial 7 part 1 must be run first**
(this notebook does not downsample). The object needs the metadata columns
`params$celltype.col`, `params$condition.col` and `params$sample.col`.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 1.1-1.12 and the
sanity checks of its "Common Pitfalls" section). Changes made for this notebook
series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter, paths built from
`params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or `FIX:` in
comments. Base-graphics plots are saved to PNG as in the article and shown in
the notebook with `knitr::include_graphics()`. The slow steps are
`computeCommunProb()`, `selectK()` / `identifyCommunicationPatterns()` (NMF)
and `netEmbedding()` / `netClustering()`.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.1: Load Libraries and Data
#-----------------------------------------------
library(CellChat)
library(Seurat)
library(patchwork)
library(NMF)        # required by selectK and identifyCommunicationPatterns
library(foreach)    # required by NMF parallel backend
library(ggalluvial) # required by netAnalysis_river (river/Sankey plots)
library(reticulate) # required by netEmbedding (Python UMAP via umap-learn)

if (!exists("params") || !is.list(params)) {
  # Running interactively (e.g. via "Run Cell") rather than through
  # knit/render, so `params` was never created by rmarkdown::render().
  # Reconstruct it by parsing this .Rmd's own YAML header, so the params
  # defaults live in exactly one place (the YAML block above) instead of
  # being duplicated here.
  rmd_path <- tryCatch(
    # Only reliable when this document is the active editor tab; if focus
    # has moved to another file, this will pick up the wrong path.
    rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path,
    error = function(e) NA_character_
  )
  if (is.na(rmd_path) || !nzchar(rmd_path)) {
    # Fallback if rstudioapi is unavailable or no doc is focused; assumes
    # the working directory is the project root.
    rmd_path <- "scRNAseq_tutorial_9_cell_communication_cellchat/tut9_cell_communication_cellchat_part1.Rmd"
  }
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(rmd_path)$params
}

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
cc.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$cellchat.subdir)

# Set up the Python environment for netEmbedding().
# virtualenv_create() is safe to call every run — it does nothing if the env exists.
# ADDED: wrapped in tryCatch so a Python/network problem does not stop the notebook;
# only netEmbedding() (Step 1.11) needs this environment.
tryCatch({
  virtualenv_create(params$reticulate.env)
  virtualenv_install(params$reticulate.env, packages = unlist(params$reticulate.packages))
  use_virtualenv(params$reticulate.env, required = TRUE)
}, error = function(e) {
  message("ADDED: Python environment setup failed (netEmbedding() in Step 1.11 will fail ",
          "unless umap-learn is available): ", conditionMessage(e))
})

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Force NMF to run sequentially — prevents "none of the packages are loaded" errors
# that occur when NMF spawns parallel worker processes with empty environments
registerDoSEQ()

# Create output directories for all saved plots
plot.dir.healthy <- file.path(cc.dir, "plots/healthy")
dir.create(plot.dir.healthy,    recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(cc.dir, "plots/comparison"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# ADDED: hand-off directory
dir.create(file.path(cc.dir, "results"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

set.seed(params$seed)

# Column names from params
celltype.col <- params$celltype.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col
sample.col <- params$sample.col

# ADDED: show PNG files written by the base-graphics plots below in the notebook
show_png <- function(...) knitr::include_graphics(path.expand(c(...)))
```

## Load the downsampled Seurat object

```{r step1_1_load_data}
# Load the downsampled annotated Seurat object from Part 7 / Part 7-2
# FIX: the article's seurat_subset.rds is not written by any notebook in this
# series; the tutorial 7 part 1 object seurat_subset_downsampled.rds is used instead.
input.file <- file.path(base.dir, params$input.subdir, params$input.rds)
# ADDED: stop with a clear message if tutorial 7 part 1 has not been run
stopifnot(file.exists(input.file))
cat("Reading in Seurat object:", input.file, "\n")
seurat_obj <- readRDS(input.file)

# ADDED: check the metadata columns and condition needed below
stopifnot(all(c(celltype.col, condition.col, sample.col) %in% colnames(seurat_obj@meta.data)))
stopifnot(params$healthy.level %in% seurat_obj@meta.data[[condition.col]])
stopifnot(params$assay %in% Assays(seurat_obj))

# ADDED: CellChat reads the 'data' layer; join it if a Seurat v5 object keeps one layer per sample
data_layers <- Layers(seurat_obj[[params$assay]], search = "^data")
if (length(data_layers) > 1) {
  seurat_obj[[params$assay]] <- JoinLayers(seurat_obj[[params$assay]])
}

# ADDED: cell types in the input object
cat("Cell types in the input object:\n")
print(table(seurat_obj@meta.data[[celltype.col]]))

# Confirm the metadata columns available — we need 'final_annotation' and 'condition'
head(seurat_obj@meta.data)
```

## Subset to the Healthy group

```{r step1_2_subset}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.2: Subset to the Healthy Group
#-----------------------------------------------
# Subset to Healthy condition only
cells.healthy <- colnames(seurat_obj)[seurat_obj@meta.data[[condition.col]] == params$healthy.level]
seurat_healthy <- subset(seurat_obj, cells = cells.healthy)

# Confirm how many cells and which cell types remain
table(seurat_healthy@meta.data[[celltype.col]])
```

## ADDED: sanity checks before creating the CellChat object

The article lists these checks in its "Common Pitfalls" section, after the
analysis. The cell-type filter (the third check) modifies the Healthy Seurat
object, so it has to run **before** `createCellChat()` and is therefore placed
here.

```{r step1_2b_checks}
# ADDED: moved from the article's "Common Pitfalls" section (data layer, cell counts)
# Confirm the data layer contains log-normalized values (non-integer, non-zero mean)
summary(GetAssayData(seurat_healthy, assay = params$assay, layer = "data")@x)[3]  # median should be > 0
# ADDED: stop if the layer is empty or all zero
stopifnot(summary(GetAssayData(seurat_healthy, assay = params$assay, layer = "data")@x)[3] > 0)

# Check cell counts per cell type
table(seurat_healthy@meta.data[[celltype.col]])

# Remove cell types with fewer than 10 cells before creating the CellChat object
keep_types <- names(which(table(seurat_healthy@meta.data[[celltype.col]]) >= params$keep.min_cells))
cells.keep <- colnames(seurat_healthy)[seurat_healthy@meta.data[[celltype.col]] %in% keep_types]
seurat_healthy <- subset(seurat_healthy, cells = cells.keep)
# ADDED: report what is left
cat("Cell types kept:", paste(keep_types, collapse = ", "), "\n")
table(seurat_healthy@meta.data[[celltype.col]])
```

## Create the CellChat object

```{r step1_3_createcellchat}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.3: Create the CellChat Object Directly from the Seurat Object
#-----------------------------------------------
# Map sample_id to the 'samples' column that CellChat v2 expects
# Must be a factor — CellChat will warn and coerce it if not
seurat_healthy$samples <- factor(seurat_healthy@meta.data[[sample.col]])

# Set the cell identities to final_annotation before creating CellChat object
Idents(seurat_healthy) <- celltype.col

# Create CellChat object directly from the Seurat object
# CellChat automatically extracts the normalized data from the RNA assay
cellchat_healthy <- createCellChat(
  object   = seurat_healthy,
  group.by = celltype.col,  # metadata column for cell type grouping
  assay    = params$assay   # use the RNA assay (log-normalized data)
)
```

## Set the ligand-receptor database

```{r step1_4_db}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.4: Set the Ligand-Receptor Database
#-----------------------------------------------
# Use the ligand-receptor interaction database of the chosen species (article: human)
CellChatDB <- get(paste0("CellChatDB.", params$db.species))

# Option A: Use all interaction categories (recommended for most analyses)
cellchat_healthy@DB <- CellChatDB

# Option B: Use only secreted signaling (uncomment if you want a focused analysis)
# cellchat_healthy@DB <- subsetDB(CellChatDB, search = "Secreted Signaling")
# ADDED: Option B is selected with params$db.subset instead of uncommenting
if (nzchar(params$db.subset)) {
  cellchat_healthy@DB <- subsetDB(CellChatDB, search = params$db.subset)
}
```

## Preprocess expression data

```{r step1_5_preprocess}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.5: Preprocess Expression Data
#-----------------------------------------------
# Step 1: Subset to genes in the database — reduces computation time
cellchat_healthy <- subsetData(cellchat_healthy)

# Step 2: Identify over-expressed signaling genes in each cell group
# do.fast = FALSE uses the standard Wilcoxon test — avoids needing the presto package,
# which frequently fails to compile on macOS. Speed difference is negligible at this dataset size.
cellchat_healthy <- identifyOverExpressedGenes(cellchat_healthy, do.fast = params$do.fast)

# Step 3: Identify over-expressed ligand-receptor interactions
cellchat_healthy <- identifyOverExpressedInteractions(cellchat_healthy)
```

## Infer the cell-cell communication network

```{r step1_6_commprob}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.6: Infer the Cell-Cell Communication Network
#-----------------------------------------------
# Compute communication probability for each ligand-receptor pair
# nboot: number of permutations for statistical testing (100 is sufficient for exploration)
cellchat_healthy <- computeCommunProb(cellchat_healthy, type = params$prob.type, nboot = params$nboot)

# Filter out communications with fewer than 10 cells in either the sender or receiver group
cellchat_healthy <- filterCommunication(cellchat_healthy, min.cells = params$min.cells)
```

## Aggregate at the signaling pathway level

```{r step1_7_aggregate}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.7: Aggregate at the Signaling Pathway Level
#-----------------------------------------------
# Infer communications at the pathway level
cellchat_healthy <- computeCommunProbPathway(cellchat_healthy)

# Calculate aggregated interaction counts and total communication strength
cellchat_healthy <- aggregateNet(cellchat_healthy)
```

## Overview: number of interactions and interaction strength

```{r step1_9_1_overview}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.9.1: Overview: Number of Interactions and Interaction Strength
#-----------------------------------------------
# Set group sizes for visualization (number of cells per cell type)
groupSize <- as.numeric(table(cellchat_healthy@idents))

png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "01a_interaction_count.png"), width = 700, height = 700, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_circle(
  cellchat_healthy@net$count,
  vertex.weight = groupSize,       # node size proportional to cell count
  weight.scale  = TRUE,
  label.edge    = FALSE,
  title.name    = "Number of Interactions"
)
invisible(dev.off())

png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "01b_interaction_strength.png"), width = 700, height = 700, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_circle(
  cellchat_healthy@net$weight,
  vertex.weight = groupSize,
  weight.scale  = TRUE,
  label.edge    = FALSE,
  title.name    = "Interaction Strength"
)
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: show the saved plots
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "01a_interaction_count.png"))
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "01b_interaction_strength.png"))
```

## Explore a specific signaling pathway

```{r step1_9_2_pathway_hierarchy}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.9.2: Explore a Specific Signaling Pathway
#-----------------------------------------------
# Check which signaling pathways are active in this dataset
cellchat_healthy@netP$pathways

# Visualize a specific pathway — MHC-II antigen presentation
pathways.show <- params$pathway.show
# ADDED: stop early if the pathway is not active in this dataset
stopifnot(pathways.show %in% cellchat_healthy@netP$pathways)

# ADDED: the hierarchy receivers are indices into the cell-type levels; show which cell types they are
levels(cellchat_healthy@idents)
cat("Hierarchy receivers:", levels(cellchat_healthy@idents)[unlist(params$hierarchy.receivers)], "\n")

# Hierarchy plot: directional view of which senders communicate to a pre-defined
# FIX: this comment is truncated in the article; it means a pre-defined set of receiver cell types.
png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "02_MHCII_hierarchy.png"), width = 1400, height = 900, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_aggregate(
  cellchat_healthy,
  signaling        = pathways.show,
  vertex.receiver  = unlist(params$hierarchy.receivers),       # B cells (index 1) and CD4+ T cells (index 2)
  layout           = "hierarchy"
)
invisible(dev.off())
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "02_MHCII_hierarchy.png"))
```

How to read the hierarchy plot (the article gives this as a text diagram,
`Source (pink) ──► Target ◄── Source (green)`): arrows point from a source
cell type to a target cell type, and sources of the two groups are drawn in
different colors (pink and green). The cell types given in
`params$hierarchy.receivers` are the pre-defined receivers.

```{r step1_9_2_pathway_circle_chord}
# Circle plot of the same pathway
png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "03_MHCII_circle.png"), width = 900, height = 900, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_aggregate(
  cellchat_healthy,
  signaling = pathways.show,
  layout    = "circle"
)
invisible(dev.off())

# Chord diagram — shows all interactions in the pathway
png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "04_MHCII_chord.png"), width = 1800, height = 1800, res = params$plot.dpi)
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
netVisual_aggregate(
  cellchat_healthy,
  signaling = pathways.show,
  layout    = "chord"
)
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: show the saved plots
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "03_MHCII_circle.png"))
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "04_MHCII_chord.png"))
```

## Contribution of individual ligand-receptor pairs

```{r step1_9_3_lr_contribution}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.9.3: Contribution of Individual Ligand-Receptor Pairs
#-----------------------------------------------
# Show the relative contribution of each L-R pair to the MHC-II pathway (ranked by communication probability)
contrib_gg <- netAnalysis_contribution(cellchat_healthy, signaling = pathways.show)
png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "05_MHCII_LR_contribution.png"), width = 900, height = 750, res = params$plot.dpi)
print(contrib_gg)
invisible(dev.off())

# Visualize a specific L-R pair (e.g., the top contributing pair, ranked by Expression enrichment score)
pairLR <- extractEnrichedLR(cellchat_healthy, signaling = pathways.show, geneLR.return = FALSE)
# ADDED: stop if there is no enriched L-R pair for this pathway
stopifnot(nrow(pairLR) >= 1)

# Visualize the top pair
png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "06_MHCII_top_LR_pair.png"), width = 900, height = 900, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_individual(
  cellchat_healthy,
  signaling    = pathways.show,
  pairLR.use   = pairLR[1, ],    # first (strongest) L-R pair
  layout       = "circle"
)
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: show the saved plots
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "05_MHCII_LR_contribution.png"))
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "06_MHCII_top_LR_pair.png"))
```

## Bubble plot: all active interactions at once

```{r step1_9_4_bubble}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.9.4: Bubble Plot: All Active Interactions at Once
#-----------------------------------------------
# Bubble plot: all significant L-R pairs
# Each bubble = one L-R interaction; x-axis = cell-type pair; y-axis = L-R pair

png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "07_bubble_all_interactions.png"), width = 1650, height = 1350, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_bubble(
  cellchat_healthy,
  remove.isolate = FALSE,    # include cell types with no interactions

# ADDED: show the saved plot

```

## Gene expression distribution of signaling genes

```{r step1_9_5_gene_expression}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.9.5: Gene Expression Distribution of Signaling Genes
#-----------------------------------------------
# Extract the ligand and receptor genes for the MHC-II pathway
# subsetCommunication() returns a data frame with 'ligand' and 'receptor' columns
mhcii_lr    <- subsetCommunication(cellchat_healthy, signaling = pathways.show)
mhcii_genes <- unique(c(mhcii_lr$ligand, mhcii_lr$receptor))

# Height scales with number of genes: 750 px per row of 3
plot_height <- 750 * ceiling(length(mhcii_genes) / 3)

# VlnPlot on seurat_healthy uses properly joined, log-normalised data
# print() is required to render the patchwork object inside png()/dev.off()
png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "08_MHCII_gene_expression.png"), width = 1500, height = plot_height, res = params$plot.dpi)
print(
  VlnPlot(
    seurat_healthy,
    features = mhcii_genes,
    group.by = celltype.col,
    pt.size  = 0,                      # hide individual dots for clarity
    ncol     = 3
  ) & theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
)
invisible(dev.off())
# ADDED: show the saved plot
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "08_MHCII_gene_expression.png"))
```

## Systems-level analysis: dominant senders and receivers

```{r step1_9_systems}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.9: Systems-Level Analysis: Who Are the Dominant Senders and Receivers?
#-----------------------------------------------
# Calculate network centrality scores
# This assigns each cell type a role: sender, receiver, mediator, or influencer
cellchat_healthy <- netAnalysis_computeCentrality(cellchat_healthy, slot.name = "netP")

# Visualize signaling roles as a heatmap
# Rows = signaling pathways; Columns = cell types; Color = centrality score
png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "09_signaling_role_heatmap_outgoing.png"), width = 1200, height = 1000, res = params$plot.dpi)
netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(
  cellchat_healthy,
  pattern  = "outgoing",      # "outgoing" = sending cells; "incoming" = receiving cells
  height   = 12
)
invisible(dev.off())

# 2D scatter plot: dominant senders vs receivers
# Cells in the upper right are both strong senders AND receivers
png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "10_signaling_role_scatter.png"), width = 900, height = 750, res = params$plot.dpi)
netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(cellchat_healthy)
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: show the saved plots
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "09_signaling_role_heatmap_outgoing.png"))
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "10_signaling_role_scatter.png"))
```

## Identify global communication patterns

Patterns are found with NMF. `selectK()` plots two quality measures (cophenetic
and silhouette) against the number of patterns K; K is chosen where they begin
to drop. The K values in `params$npatterns.outgoing` (5) and
`params$npatterns.incoming` (6) are the article's choices for its data, made by
eye from these plots, so **review the two selectK PNGs and adjust the params
for this input object** before relying on the patterns. This step is slow.

```{r step1_10_outgoing_selectk}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.10: Identify Global Communication Patterns
#-----------------------------------------------
# Identify outgoing communication patterns (how senders coordinate)

# registerDoSEQ() forces NMF to run sequentially instead of spawning parallel worker to avoid errors
registerDoSEQ()

png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "11_selectK_outgoing.png"), width = 900, height = 700, res = params$plot.dpi)
selectK(cellchat_healthy, pattern = "outgoing")
invisible(dev.off())
# ADDED: show the saved plot
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "11_selectK_outgoing.png"))
```

```{r step1_10_outgoing_patterns}
# K=5 selected for outgoing (params$npatterns.outgoing; the article's choice)
nPatterns <- params$npatterns.outgoing

# registerDoSEQ() must be set again for the same reason
registerDoSEQ()

cellchat_healthy <- identifyCommunicationPatterns(
  cellchat_healthy,
  pattern   = "outgoing",
  k         = nPatterns,
  height    = 18
)
```

```{r step1_10_outgoing_plots}
png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "12_pattern_river_outgoing.png"), width = 1200, height = 900, res = params$plot.dpi)
netAnalysis_river(cellchat_healthy, pattern = "outgoing")
invisible(dev.off())

png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "13_pattern_dot_outgoing.png"), width = 1200, height = 1050, res = params$plot.dpi)
netAnalysis_dot(cellchat_healthy, pattern = "outgoing")
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: show the saved plots
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "12_pattern_river_outgoing.png"))
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "13_pattern_dot_outgoing.png"))
```

```{r step1_10_incoming_selectk}
# Repeat the same workflow for incoming patterns (receiver coordination)
registerDoSEQ()

png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "14_selectK_incoming.png"), width = 900, height = 700, res = params$plot.dpi)
selectK(cellchat_healthy, pattern = "incoming")
invisible(dev.off())
# ADDED: show the saved plot
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "14_selectK_incoming.png"))
```

```{r step1_10_incoming_patterns}
# Review plots/healthy/14_selectK_incoming.png before setting nPatterns.
# (params$npatterns.incoming; the article's choice is 6)
nPatterns <- params$npatterns.incoming

registerDoSEQ()

cellchat_healthy <- identifyCommunicationPatterns(
  cellchat_healthy,
  pattern   = "incoming",
  k         = nPatterns,
  height    = 18
)
```

```{r step1_10_incoming_plots}
png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "15_pattern_river_incoming.png"), width = 1200, height = 900, res = params$plot.dpi)
netAnalysis_river(cellchat_healthy, pattern = "incoming")
invisible(dev.off())

png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "16_pattern_dot_incoming.png"), width = 1200, height = 1050, res = params$plot.dpi)
netAnalysis_dot(cellchat_healthy, pattern = "incoming")
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: show the saved plots
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "15_pattern_river_incoming.png"))
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "16_pattern_dot_incoming.png"))
```

## Identify functionally similar signaling pathways

`netEmbedding()` uses Python UMAP (umap-learn) through reticulate; see the
Python environment set up at the top of this notebook.

```{r step1_11_similarity}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1.11: Identify Functionally Similar Signaling Pathways
#-----------------------------------------------
# Group pathways by functional similarity (similar sender-receiver structures)
cellchat_healthy <- computeNetSimilarity(cellchat_healthy, type = "functional")
cellchat_healthy <- netEmbedding(cellchat_healthy, type = "functional")

options(future.rng.onMisuse = "ignore")
cellchat_healthy <- netClustering(cellchat_healthy, type = "functional")

# Visualize pathway groups in 2D embedding
png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "17_pathway_functional_embedding.png"), width = 1050, height = 900, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_embedding(cellchat_healthy, type = "functional", label.size = 3.5)
invisible(dev.off())

png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "18_pathway_functional_embedding_zoom.png"), width = 1050, height = 900, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_embeddingZoomIn(cellchat_healthy, type = "functional", nCol = 2)
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: show the saved plots
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "17_pathway_functional_embedding.png"))
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.healthy, "18_pathway_functional_embedding_zoom.png"))
```
